draft.title: Substituting into formulas
card: A formula links quantities with pronumerals, such as \(v = u + at\). To use it, replace each pronumeral you know with its value. Put the value in brackets if it is negative.
After substituting, you have an equation with one unknown. Solve it with inverse operations, as you would any linear equation.
Example: use \(v = u + at\) to find \(a\) when \(v = 20\), \(u = 8\) and \(t = 3\). Substitute to get \(20 = 8 + 3a\).
Subtract 8 from both sides: \(12 = 3a\). Divide both sides by 3: \(a = 4\). Check by putting 4 back into the formula: \(8 + 3 \times 4 = 20\).
draft.remember: Substitute the known values first, then solve the equation for the unknown.

a.q: In \(v = u + at\), \(v = 25\), \(u = 7\) and \(a = 2\). Which equation results from substituting?
a.why: Each known value replaces its own pronumeral, so \(v\) becomes 25, \(u\) becomes 7 and \(a\) becomes 2, which leaves \(25 = 7 + 2t\). Swapping the values of \(u\) and \(a\) gives \(25 = 2 + 7t\), which is a tempting mistake.
a.clue: Match each value to its own pronumeral.

b.q: The formula \(P = 2l + 2w\) gives the perimeter of a rectangle. A rectangle has \(P = 30\) and \(l = 9\). What is \(w\)?
b.why: Substitute to get \(30 = 2 \times 9 + 2w\), so \(30 = 18 + 2w\). Subtract 18 to get \(12 = 2w\), then divide by 2 to get \(w = 6\). The answer \(w = 12\) forgets to divide by 2 at the end.
